report:
## Conclusion: Yes — with an important caveat about who benefits

Strong evidence supports that corticosteroids like dexamethasone reduce mortality specifically in critically ill (severely hypoxic or ventilated) COVID-19 patients — but not in mild cases.

**Key evidence:**

1. **RECOVERY Trial (Oxford, published in NEJM)** — This large randomized controlled trial in hospitalized UK patients found dexamethasone (6mg/day for up to 10 days) reduced 28-day mortality by about one-third in patients on invasive mechanical ventilation, and by about one-fifth in patients needing supplemental oxygen alone. Critically, there was **no mortality benefit — and possibly harm — in patients who did not require oxygen support**. (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2021436)

2. **WHO REACT Working Group Meta-analysis (JAMA, 2020)** — This prospective meta-analysis pooled data from 7 randomized trials (including RECOVERY, plus others like the hydrocortisone trials) covering critically ill COVID-19 patients. It confirmed that systemic corticosteroid administration was associated with lower 28-day all-cause mortality compared to usual care/placebo, reinforcing the RECOVERY findings across multiple independent trials and steroid types (dexamethasone, hydrocortisone, methylprednisolone). (https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2770279)

3. **Corroborating meta-analyses** — Subsequent systematic reviews and meta-analyses (e.g., PMC7897363) pooling ~6,250 severe COVID-19 patients across 7 RCTs found corticosteroids reduced all-cause mortality and disease progression without significantly increasing serious adverse events, further validating the finding. (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7897363/)

**Bottom line:** The evidence — from large RCTs and pooled meta-analyses — robustly supports that corticosteroids increase survival in critically ill/severe COVID-19 patients requiring oxygen or ventilation, but they show no benefit (and may be harmful) in patients with mild disease not needing respiratory support.
